## Revised credibility argument

FRONTLINE publishes journalistic guidelines that bind it on the two points that matter here: its funder clause states that the editorial integrity of a programme demands that the funder not become part of the editorial process, and a separate clause requires a fact-checking procedure on completion of every programme. Its editorial standards page adopts those guidelines, names its editor-in-chief, lists its funders, sets out corrections, and records Trust Project membership. Elected lower house of the Parliament of Canada. It publishes verbatim evidence given to its committees.

Standing Order 108(1)(a) gives Canadian House of Commons committees the power to send for persons, papers and records, and House procedure allows a committee to summon a witness who is unwilling to appear, with enforcement a matter for the House itself rather than the committee. The Evidence we cite is the committee's own published record of its meeting of 18 November 2009, at which the diplomat Richard Colvin gave his account of detainee transfers. It is the edited and revised transcript rather than a raw verbatim one, the record does not show the witness was sworn, and a committee is not a court, so evidence is not tested by cross-examination. His account was contested, and we cite it as testimony given to Parliament.

nodes.text: The papers state their limits plainly, saying the totals are a substantial undercount, and the project names its funders, which include Carnegie Corporation and Open Society foundations. Its Afghan casualty figures come from more than one source: the paper we cite uses Crawford's own earlier estimates for 2001 to 2007, UNAMA's protection of civilians reporting for 2008 to 2021, and New York Times reporting for July 2021. For the UNAMA years it is therefore an analysis built on UNAMA rather than independent confirmation of it, and its description of a two-independent-source threshold characterises the upstream sources it draws on rather than a rule it applies itself. The lead author on that work is one of the project's co-directors.

Investigative documentary series produced by GBH Boston for PBS since 1983. It publishes full interview transcripts alongside its films.

FRONTLINE publishes journalistic guidelines that bind it on the two points that matter here: its funder clause states that the editorial integrity of a programme demands that the funder not become part of the editorial process, and a separate clause requires a fact-checking procedure on completion of every programme. Its editorial standards page adopts those guidelines, names its editor-in-chief, lists its funders, sets out corrections, and records Trust Project membership. It also publishes the full transcript of the documentary we cite, so the broadcast can be checked line by line. These are adopted policies, not proof of compliance in any one programme.
